points.description: States that both iteration and recursion involve repetition (repeated execution of a set of statements / doing something over and over). Accept everyday wording such as 'both repeat steps' or 'both loop/repeat code'.

levels.says: Mentions repetition or looping as a feature of both, but the wording is vague or only implies it (e.g. 'both do the same thing again') without making clear that both involve repeated execution.

points.description: States that both have a termination test / stopping condition (a condition that ends the repetition, such as a base case in recursion or a loop condition in iteration). Accept 'both need a way to stop' or 'both have a condition that ends them'.

levels.says: Says both must stop or end at some point, but does not mention a test/condition/base case that controls termination.

points.description: States that both can occur infinitely (both can fail to terminate / can loop forever if the termination condition is never met). Accept 'both can be infinite' or 'both can run forever'.

levels.says: Mentions infinite looping or non-termination but attaches it to only one of iteration or recursion, or states it unclearly.

rubric.notes: Full marks require all three similarities: both involve repetition, both have a termination test, and both can occur infinitely. Part marks are given where a similarity is present but vague or incomplete, as set out in the levels. No marks are given for a point that is absent or that describes a difference rather than a similarity.
